bd.reimbursement: Facility: the disposable kit is packaged into the procedure; CPT 38220/38222 (marrow aspiration) and 20939 (bone marrow aspiration for bone grafting, add-on) exist for the surgeon but many payers deny 20939 or bundle it. Office/injection use of BMAC for musculoskeletal conditions is generally non-covered by Medicare.
bd.notes: Arthrex (Angel), Zimmer Biomet, Stryker and Terumo all sell concentration disposables through their foot/ankle or sports-medicine reps; the kit is cheap relative to a cellular allograft, which is the main commercial argument in ASCs.

products.name: Platelet-rich plasma / platelet concentrate (point-of-care)
products.company: Multiple (Arthrex ACP, Zimmer Biomet GPS, Harvest/Terumo, EmCyte and others)
products.ownership_history: Not applicable; many 510(k)-cleared concentration systems.
products.composition: Autologous platelet concentrate (with or without leukocytes) prepared by centrifugation; applied to the fusion bed or injected

regulatory.reference: Systems cleared for preparing platelet-rich plasma from autologous blood, typically to be mixed with autograft or allograft bone; no cleared bone-healing claim; Cleared by CBER under product code ORG 'platelet and plasma separator for bone graft handling' (21 CFR 864.9245), e.g., Arthrex ACP Max BK210655 (2022-09-22), Arthrex Angel BK180180 (2018-07-05), Isto Precise BK200540 (2022-03-17), RegenLab RegenKit-THT BK090048 (2010-05-18, product code FMF), and older CDRH centrifuges (JQC); labeling is PRP for mixing with bone graft to improve handling, no fracture-healing indication
on_label_indications: Preparation of autologous PRP for mixing with bone graft materials (typical 510(k) wording); no fusion or fracture-healing indication

applications.evidence_summary: Weak evidence. Bibbo 2010 (PMID 21056862) reviewed 'only a handful' of basic-science and clinical foot/ankle PRP papers; a prospective Arthrex ACP ankle-arthrodesis study (NCT01131455) was terminated after 10 patients; Bolia 2024 (PMID 38704857) rated the arthrodesis PRP evidence as low quality.
applications.caveats: No RCT shows PRP improves foot/ankle fusion; the only positive high-risk series combined PRP with marrow aspirate (Pinzur 2009).

applications.evidence_summary: Pinzur 2009 (PMID 19254506) used platelet-rich concentrate plus marrow aspirate in 46 Charcot feet with 42 unions; PRP's independent contribution is unknown.
applications.caveats: Confounded single-arm series.

evidence.title: Platelet-rich plasma concentrate to augment bone fusion
evidence.finding: Review: only a handful of foot/ankle PRP papers; proposes a risk classification for when to augment.

evidence.title: Autologous concentrated platelet-rich plasma (Arthrex ACP) for local application in ankle arthrodesis
evidence.finding: Terminated after 10 patients; no results posted.

evidence.title: Comparative studies of bone graft and orthobiologics for foot ankle arthrodesis: a critical review
evidence.finding: Critical review of autograft, allograft, DBM, calcium sulfate/phosphate, rhBMP-2, rhPDGF-BB, PRP and BMAC in ankle/hindfoot arthrodesis emphasizing low quality of evidence for most.

bd.reimbursement: Facility kit packaged; Medicare covers PRP (CPT 0232T) only for chronic non-healing diabetic wounds under coverage-with-evidence-development, not for fusion or fracture; cash-pay in clinics.
bd.notes: Sold by sports-medicine reps; in fusion surgery it is an inexpensive add-on with no evidence lever, so it rarely features in biologics contracting.

products.name: Amniotic and placental tissue products (dHACM injectables, amnion sheets and tendon wraps; e.g., MiMedx AmnioFix/EpiFix, Organogenesis, Integra and others)
products.company: Multiple (MiMedx, Organogenesis, Integra, Smith+Nephew, BioTissue and many tissue banks)
products.ownership_history: Fragmented; MiMedx is the largest US amnion processor.
products.composition: Dehydrated or cryopreserved human amnion/chorion membrane, as sheets (wraps/barriers) or micronized powder reconstituted for injection; some products are flowable amniotic fluid or umbilical-cord derived

regulatory.reference: Sheet forms used as a covering or barrier are regulated as 361 HCT/Ps when minimally manipulated and homologous. Micronized or injectable forms used to treat tendinopathy, fasciitis or arthritis do not meet the 361 criteria and require a BLA; FDA's enforcement-discretion period for such products ended 2021-05-31, and MiMedx stated that AmnioFix Injectable, EpiFix Micronized and AmnioFill were affected while its sheet products were not.
on_label_indications: Sheet products: homologous use as a wound covering or barrier (no FDA-reviewed therapeutic indication)
Injectable/micronized products for plantar fasciitis or tendinopathy: no FDA approval; investigational (IND/BLA) only after 2021

applications.evidence_summary: Plantar fasciitis injection, not bone healing: Cazzell 2018 (PMID 30058377) 14-site RCT, 145 patients, single micronized dHACM injection vs saline; VAS fell 76% vs 45% at 3 months (p<0.0001). Zelen 2013 (PMID 23945520) 45-patient RCT positive at 8 weeks; Hanselman 2014 (PMID 25249320) cryopreserved amnion vs corticosteroid, 23 patients, mostly no difference. Network meta-analysis of 22 injection RCTs (PMID 27143138) found dHACM superior to corticosteroid only in the short term with no data beyond 2 months.
applications.caveats: MiMedx-funded trials with company authors; the injectable products studied are no longer lawfully marketed without a BLA; no evidence for bone healing in the foot. Tendon-wrap use (Achilles, peroneal) rests on case series. Tiered investigational per FDA position.

evidence.title: Randomized controlled trial of micronized dehydrated human amnion/chorion membrane (dHACM) injection compared to placebo for the treatment of plantar fasciitis
evidence.finding: 76% VAS reduction vs 45% placebo at 3 months; FFI-R improved 60% vs 40%.

evidence.title: Prospective, randomized, blinded, comparative study of injectable micronized dehydrated amniotic/chorionic membrane allograft for plantar fasciitis
evidence.finding: AOFAS hindfoot score improved 51-53 points with mDHACM vs 13 points with saline at 8 weeks.

evidence.title: Cryopreserved human amniotic membrane injection for plantar fasciitis: a randomized, controlled, double-blind pilot study
evidence.finding: Mostly no difference vs corticosteroid; pilot.

evidence.title: Injection therapies for plantar fasciopathy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of 22 randomised controlled trials
evidence.finding: Dehydrated amniotic membrane superior to corticosteroid at 0-2 months; no data beyond 2 months.

bd.reimbursement: Facility use (wraps in surgery) is packaged with no separate payment. Office injections billed under product-specific Q-codes have been targeted by Medicare contractors with overpayment demands since 2022; Medicare treats non-wound orthopedic amniotic injections as not reasonable and necessary, and CMS's CY2026 physician fee schedule overhauled skin-substitute payment (details not verified in this sweep). Commercial payers largely exclude amniotic injections as experimental.
bd.notes: Sold by wound-care and podiatry reps; the post-2021 market is sheet products for wounds and surgical wraps. Any BD plan treating injectable amnion as an orthopedic product must assume BLA-level development; MiMedx has pursued IND-based trials for its injectable.

products.name: Structural allograft (femoral head, bulk tricortical and shaped allograft wedges)
products.company: Tissue banks (MTF Biologics, AlloSource, LifeNet Health, RTI/Surgalign successors) and hardware companies that private-label allograft wedges
products.ownership_history: Not applicable.
products.composition: Fresh-frozen or freeze-dried human femoral head or cortical-cancellous block, shaped intraoperatively or supplied as preformed wedges (Cotton, Evans, interposition)

regulatory.reference: none
on_label_indications: Homologous use as structural bone graft; no FDA-reviewed indication

applications.evidence_summary: Cifaldi 2022 (PMID 35585002): systematic review of 11 studies, 175 patients with TTC arthrodesis and structural allograft (mostly femoral head with a retrograde nail); union 67.4%, limb salvage 92.5%, complications 26.6%, allograft collapse 1.2%. Jeng 2013 (PMID 23650649): 32 patients, 50% radiographic fusion, every diabetic patient a nonunion, 19% below-knee amputation, 71% functional limb salvage counting asymptomatic nonunions.
applications.caveats: High nonunion despite high limb salvage; 3D-printed titanium cages now report 88-89% pooled union (PMID 41724588, PMID 42600975) and one comparative study favored the cage over femoral head for fusion and subsidence.

applications.evidence_summary: Femoral-head and bulk allograft used to restore medial-column length after wedge resection; PMID 34677103 reported high fusion in 14 bone-block TTC fusions with allograft plus BMAC plus DBM and prolonged protected weight-bearing.
applications.caveats: Small series; Charcot subgroup outcomes worse.

applications.evidence_summary: Interposition allograft block for salvage of failed first MTP implant arthroplasty; pooled nonunion 16.5% across 76 patients (PMID 37165627).
applications.caveats: Six level-IV studies.

applications.evidence_summary: Preformed allograft wedges are the most common Cotton and Evans osteotomy spacer; no comparative outcome data found.
applications.caveats: Expert practice.

evidence.title: Tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis with structural allograft for management of large osseous defects of the hindfoot and ankle: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Union 67.4%, limb salvage 92.5%; no difference nail vs plate.

evidence.title: Tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis with bulk femoral head allograft for salvage of large defects in the ankle
evidence.finding: 50% fusion; diabetes the only predictor of nonunion; 19% amputation.

evidence.title: Tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis using a novel retrograde intramedullary nail
evidence.finding: 70% fusion overall; 76.5% in the 17 patients needing femoral-head allograft.

evidence.title: Patient-specific 3D-printed porous titanium implants for complex foot and ankle reconstruction: a current concepts review
evidence.finding: Pooled union 89%, limb salvage 92%, reoperation 26%; the single comparative study favored the cage over femoral-head allograft.

bd.reimbursement: No separate payment; bundled or packaged. Allograft is usually procured under the hospital's tissue-bank agreement.
bd.notes: Commodity-priced; the competitive threat is custom 3D-printed titanium (restor3d, 4WEB, Paragon 28/Zimmer Biomet) which carries a much higher ASP and is displacing femoral head in TTC salvage at academic centers.

products.name: Bioactive glass bone void fillers and wedges (NovaBone 45S5, Bio2 Vitrium, Treace VitaFuse, BonAlive S53P4 and others)
products.company: Multiple (NovaBone/Isto Biologics, Bio2 Technologies, Treace Medical, BonAlive Biomaterials, Stryker Vitoss BA)
products.ownership_history: Treace Medical introduced VitaFuse Bioactive Glass Graft in its 2026 AOFAS portfolio update as the newest addition to its biologics line (beside the tissue-based CortiFuse graft). BonAlive S53P4 is CE-marked for osteomyelitis in Europe; its US status for that use was not verified.
products.composition: Silicate (45S5, S53P4) or borate bioactive glass granules, putties, fiber scaffolds and machined wedges that form a hydroxycarbonate apatite layer and release ions; S53P4 has intrinsic antibacterial activity

regulatory.reference: Per brand: NovaBone putty K240404 (2024-03-05) and K242299 (2024-09-25); Bio2 CLM BG Bioactive Scaffold K142463 (2014-12-18) and K152589 (2016-01-12); Bonalive K231528 (2023-07-11); Vitoss BA K103173/K163621. Treace VitaFuse: no 510(k) found in openFDA under that name or under applicant Treace (searched 2026-10-22) - may be marketed under another clearance or as a different sponsor's device
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for non-structural voids of the extremities, pelvis and posterolateral spine (class-typical); machined wedges for opening-wedge osteotomies

applications.evidence_summary: Shi 2018 (PMID 30316643): 29 high-risk patients, 48 hindfoot joints fused with bioactive glass plus bone marrow aspirate; 25% nonunion overall (16.7% subtalar).
applications.caveats: Retrospective, no comparator, a nonunion rate at the high end for hindfoot fusion.

applications.evidence_summary: Borenstein 2023 republication (PMID 37669405): 17 Cotton osteotomies with bioactive-glass wedges (Bio2), all united, one delayed union; a Bio2 employee is a co-author.
applications.caveats: Industry co-authored, 17 patients, 6.5-month follow-up.

applications.evidence_summary: De Giglio 2020 (PMID 33358382): 44 diabetic foot osteomyelitis patients, 22 with S53P4 bioactive glass after debridement vs 22 debridement alone; osteomyelitis resolution 90% vs 61.9% (p=0.03).
applications.caveats: Italian single-center retrospective; S53P4's antibacterial-use labeling is European; US use for infection is off-label.

applications.evidence_summary: Ma 2021 (PMID 33781640): 31 calcaneal tumor/cyst curettages, 45S5 Bioglass (16) vs allograft (15); faster ingrowth (3.7 vs 4.5 months) and healing with similar AOFAS scores.
applications.caveats: Cysts, not fractures.

evidence.title: Open curettage with bone augmentation for symptomatic tumors and tumor-like lesions of calcaneus: a comparison of bioactive glass versus allogeneic bone
evidence.finding: Faster bone ingrowth and wound drying with 45S5 Bioglass than allograft.

products.name: MagnetOs (granules, putty, Easypack putty)
products.ownership_history: Kuros (Schlieren, Switzerland; SIX-listed) throughout; US spine launch 2019-2020. On 2025-01-07 Kuros Biosciences USA, Inc. announced a five-year exclusive sales agency agreement under which Medtronic's spinal division acts as exclusive sales agent for MagnetOs in mutually agreed US spine territories, converting an earlier trial arrangement into a strategic alliance. Per the Kuros investor release as summarized by search (the IR page returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; the structure and term are mirrored by BoneZone and Medical Design & Development), Kuros keeps contracts, hospital partnerships and revenue recognition and may sell directly in non-contracted territories and non-spine markets. applications.caveats: No foot/ankle results yet; spine evidence is the basis for the claim.

products.name: Induce XT (Natural Matrix Protein allograft)
products.ownership_history: Red Rock Regeneration (private); NMP technology also described in a 2026 preclinical paper (PMID 42774656) from an affiliated group.
products.composition: Human cortical bone fibers and microparticulates processed into Natural Matrix Protein (NMP, a growth-factor-bioavailability-enhanced demineralized allograft) with added cancellous microparticulates

regulatory.reference: No FDA clearance or approval record found: openFDA 510(k) search for applicant 'Red Rock' returns nothing, and no HCT/P determination is public. Product is a human cortical fiber/microparticulate allograft processed into Natural Matrix Protein (NMP); the prospective foot-and-ankle fusion study NCT06662266 (n=60, started May 2025, est. completion 2027-11) is registered as not an FDA-regulated device study.
on_label_indications: No FDA-reviewed indication; homologous bone-graft use (presumed)

applications.evidence_summary: NCT06662266: prospective single-site evaluation of Induce XT in 60 foot and ankle fusions, enrolling by invitation since May 2025, primary completion November 2026.
applications.caveats: Single-arm, single-site; preclinical claim that NMP releases more BMP-7 than conventional DBM comes from the developer.

evidence.title: Prospective evaluation of Induce XT bone graft in foot and ankle fusion
evidence.finding: Enrolling by invitation.

evidence.title: A novel growth factor bioavailability-enhanced allograft for use in craniomaxillofacial bone regeneration
evidence.finding: NMP released more BMP-7 than DBM and was osteoinductive in the rat muscle pouch; competitors OsteoAMP, OsteoFactor and i-FACTOR did not form bone.

bd.reimbursement: No separate payment; bundled or packaged.
bd.notes: Small-company entrant; relevance is as a signal that 'enhanced DBM' claims are being tested in the foot first because the fusion model is small and outpatient.

products.challenge: Regulatory pathway (510(k) vs 361) is unstated by the sponsor; no FDA record exists, so the atlas should show it as unclassified/investigational rather than as a 361 product.
